item.title: Obituary: dedicated to building the South
item.description: Stew MacLeod relaxes on scaffolding surrounding the spire of Dunedin’s First Church during redevelopment in the early 1990s. Photos: supplied STEWART MACLEOD Engineer With an innate ability for machinery and engineering in the blood, Stew MacLeod had a hand in thousands of projects across Otago and New Zealand.

item.title: Obituary: Cora Weiss, activist
item.description: Cora Weiss. Photo: Wikimedia Commons Cora Weiss was one of the most prominent figures in the United States peace movement in the 1960s and was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize several times.

item.title: Obituary: Grant Batty, rugby player
item.description: Grant Batty in 1974. Photo: Getty Images Diminutive winger Grant Batty was an All Blacks star of the 1970s, as much for his dynamic rugby skills as for his stature.

item.title: Obituary: the dazzling, clever playwright who became an adjective
item.description: Tom Stoppard attends An Evening with Joe Wright at The Film Society of Lincoln Center in New York City in 2012. Photos: Getty Images SIR TOM STOPPARD Playwright "What's it about?" was a frequent response from bemused theatre-goers to Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead, Sir Tom Stoppard’s first stage triumph.
